tasks.short: Maintain a clinical practice and file the hours

steps.what: Read the clinical roster in the {CALENDAR}.
Maintain the clinical practice while caring for patients.
Write the shift note in the care record ({OTHER}).
Draft an unsaved hours sheet from that roster.
Check the date, unit and hours against the roster and accept the sheet.
File only the accepted hours sheet in the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: She reads the roster in the {CALENDAR}. A deterministic sheet copies the date, the unit and the hours and does not save and names no patient. She checks that meaning. A separate step files only the accepted sheet in the {DOCS}. She still maintains the clinical practice and still writes the shift note in the care record ({OTHER}). Nothing is sent outside.
tasks.previous_blocker: The roster and the faculty hours return lived in two places, so she retyped the dates and hours.
tasks.enabler_now: The roster already stores the date, the unit and the hours, so a sheet can copy them for her to accept or reject.
tasks.still_hard: Caring for the patient and writing the shift note stay on the ward.
tasks.human_edge: She is the clinician on that shift and sees the patient.
tasks.altitude: Her week on the ward stays. She no longer retypes the hours, but she still accepts the sheet before it is filed, and the care and the note stay hers.

reach.task: keep a clinical shift beside teaching
reach.learn: which date, unit and hours the sheet may copy, and that it must name no patient

evidence.claim: Patient care and the shift note stay with her. The only shorter work is copying the roster into an hours sheet and filing the sheet she accepted. Model knowledge.
A patient note is special-category health data. The hours sheet copies only the date, the unit and the hours, and it names no patient. Model knowledge.
Emotion inference in education has been banned since February 2025.

assumptions: The {CALENDAR} roster stores the shift date, the unit and the hours. She reads them in s1. The sheet copies only those fields. If a field is missing she types it. The sheet names no patient and states no diagnosis.
The shift note in the care record ({OTHER}) is written by her in s3 and is not an input to the sheet. Filing the sheet in the {DOCS} is inside the institution. A wording change voids the filing.
Patient care and the note are not shortened. Neither is a send outside the organisation. A letter to the hospital would be its own gated step and is not built.
The 8 already-counted hours are the check in s5 and are not subtracted again. The 4 incremental hours are rewrites when she rejects a sheet.
No step infers a patient's emotion. The sheet does not monitor staff.
unknowns: Whether the roster stores date, unit and hours as separate fields, or only as a prose note.
Whether the faculty hours return is allowed to omit the unit name.
research_questions: What share of hours sheets she rejects because a shift changed after she read the roster.

already_counted.description: Checking the date, unit and hours against the roster is already in s5.

incremental.description: Rewriting a rejected hours sheet herself, beyond the check already in s5.

approvals.approved_version: Hours sheet she accepted in s5: shift date, unit and hours copied from the roster she read, with no patient name and no diagnosis. A wording change voids it.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a week she rejects the sheet and rewrites the hours, only filing is shorter, about 3. On a week the roster is stable and she accepts the draft, writing the sheet and filing it are shorter, about 9. The 4 hours of rewrites are already off the central 16.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Serve on academic and administrative committees

steps.what: Read the papers on the academic issues in the {DOCS}.
Draft an unsaved brief of the decision asked in those papers.
Check each decision line against the paper and accept the brief.
File only the accepted brief in the {DOCS}.
Serve on the academic or administrative committees.
Speak on the institutional policies and departmental matters.

tasks.design: She reads the committee papers in the {DOCS}. A deterministic brief copies the title, the decision asked and the page and does not save and adds no vote. She checks each line. A separate step files only the accepted brief in the {DOCS}. She still serves on the committees and still speaks on the policies in the room. Nothing is sent outside.
tasks.previous_blocker: The decision line sat inside a long paper, so she retyped it before the meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: The paper already states the title, the decision asked and the page.
tasks.still_hard: What the committee should decide is a discussion in the room.
tasks.human_edge: She hears the other members and knows the department.
tasks.altitude: She still spends the meeting in the room. She no longer copies the decision line, but she still accepts the brief before it is filed, and the view stays hers.

reach.task: prepare the papers for a departmental committee
reach.learn: which decision line the brief may copy and which vote it must not add

evidence.claim: Serving on the committee and speaking in the room stay with her. The only shorter work is copying the decision line and filing the brief she accepted. Model knowledge.
Only the examination board sanctions fraud.
Emotion inference in education has been banned since February 2025.

assumptions: Each committee paper in the {DOCS} already states a title, the decision asked and a page. She reads them in s1. The brief copies only those three fields. If a field is missing she types it. The brief adds no vote.
The brief does not record a sanction or a result. Filing it in the {DOCS} is inside the institution. A wording change voids the filing.
Speaking in the committee is a talk with colleagues, not a send outside the organisation. The meeting is not shortened.
The 8 already-counted hours are the check in s3 and are not subtracted again. The 3 incremental hours are rewrites when she rejects a brief.
No step infers a person's emotion. The brief is not a record of how members vote and does not monitor staff.
unknowns: Whether committee papers state the decision asked as a separate line, or only inside continuous prose.
Whether a secretary, rather than the instructor, is the person who files the brief.
research_questions: What share of briefs she rejects because the decision asked changed after she read the paper.

already_counted.description: Checking each decision line against the paper she read is already in s3.

incremental.description: Rewriting a rejected committee brief herself, beyond the check already in s3.

approvals.approved_version: Brief she accepted in s3: title, decision asked and page copied from the paper she read, with no vote and no sanction. A wording change voids it.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a term the papers change and she rejects the brief, only filing is shorter, about 3. On a term the papers are stable, writing the brief and filing it are shorter, about 8. The 3 hours of rewrites are already off the central 14.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select and obtain textbooks and laboratory equipment

steps.what: Read the skills-lab list of needed materials in the {DOCS}.
Read the catalogue line for the textbooks and laboratory equipment.
Select the materials and supplies the course still needs.
Draft an unsaved order from the items she selected.
Check the item, quantity and code, then accept the order.
Send only the accepted order through the {PROCUREMENT} to the supplier.
Obtain the supplies and check the laboratory equipment on the bench.

tasks.design: She reads the materials list in the {DOCS} and the catalogue line in the {PROCUREMENT}, then selects the items. A deterministic order copies only those items and does not save. She checks the item, the quantity and the code. A separate step sends only the accepted order through the {PROCUREMENT}. She still checks the laboratory equipment on the bench.
tasks.previous_blocker: The list and the catalogue lived apart, so she retyped the order.
tasks.enabler_now: The catalogue already stores the item name, the code and the unit, and she has already selected the line.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the item is safe for the skills session is her judgement, and checking the delivery on the bench stays hers.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which item the session can use on a student.
tasks.altitude: She still chooses the items and still checks what arrives. She no longer retypes the order, but she accepts it before the separate send.

reach.task: collect the skills-lab list before the instructor selects
reach.learn: which item may be ordered only after the instructor has selected it

evidence.claim: Choosing the items and checking them on the bench stay with her. The only shorter work is drafting the order from her selection and sending the order she accepted. Model knowledge.
A wrong laboratory item can injure a student in a skills session. She accepts the item, the quantity and the code before the order is sent. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The materials list in the {DOCS} stores the item and the quantity. The {PROCUREMENT} catalogue stores the item name, the code and the unit. She reads both before she selects. The order copies only the lines she selected in s3. If a code is missing she types it. The order adds no substitute item.

The send in s6 is the only step that leaves the organisation. It sends the accepted version and no other. An item change voids it. Receiving the goods and checking them on the bench are not shortened and are not a send.
The order carries no patient name and does not change a clinical protocol.
The 10 already-counted hours are the check in s5 and are not subtracted again. The 5 incremental hours are rewrites when she rejects an order.
unknowns: Whether the catalogue code is already on the skills-lab list, or only in the supplier catalogue.
Whether a purchasing colleague, rather than the instructor, is allowed to release the order after she accepts it.
research_questions: What share of orders she rejects because the catalogue code did not match the item she selected.

already_counted.description: Checking the item, quantity and code against her selection and the catalogue is already in s5.

incremental.description: Rewriting a rejected supply order herself, beyond the check already in s5.

approvals.approved_version: Order she accepted in s5: item name, quantity and catalogue code she selected, with no substitute item. An item change voids it. The send uses this version and no other.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On an order she rejects and rewrites, only the send is shorter, about 4. On an order she accepts the draft, writing the order and sending it are shorter, about 10. The 5 hours of rewrites are already off the central 18.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Join nursing recruitment, registration and placement

steps.what: Read the nursing recruitment dates in the {CALENDAR}.
Read the ward rule that governs placement in the {DOCS}.
Draft an unsaved open-day card from those dates and that rule.
Check the session, time and place against the dates and the ward rule.
File only the accepted open-day card in the {DOCS}.
Participate in the student recruitment activities on the open day.
Stand at registration and tell a colleague which session is open.
Talk with the student about placement and leave the decision in the room.

tasks.design: She reads the recruitment dates in the {CALENDAR} and the ward placement rule in the {DOCS}. A deterministic card copies the session, the time and the place and does not save and names no student. She checks that meaning. A separate step files only the accepted card in the {DOCS}. She still participates in the recruitment activities, still stands at registration, and still talks about placement in the room. Nothing is sent outside.
tasks.previous_blocker: The open-day dates and the ward rule lived in two places, so she copied them by hand before each activity.
tasks.enabler_now: The calendar already stores the session, the time and the place, and the ward rule is written.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a student fits a ward is a conversation, and the placement decision is not a card.
tasks.human_edge: She is in the room with the student and knows the ward.
tasks.altitude: The open day and the placement talk stay hers. She no longer copies the dates, but she accepts the card before it is filed, and she does not admit or place anyone from the card.

reach.task: stand at a student recruitment activity
reach.learn: which session fact must be on the card, and that the card must not admit or place a student

evidence.claim: The open day, the registration talk and the placement conversation stay with her. The only shorter work is copying the dates onto a card and filing the card she accepted. Model knowledge.
Annex III point 3 covers admission, evaluating learning outcomes, setting the education level, and detecting cheating in tests.
Emotion inference in education has been banned since February 2025.

assumptions: The {CALENDAR} stores the session, the time and the place. The ward rule in the {DOCS} is already written. She reads both before the card is drafted. The card copies those fields and names no student. If a field is missing she types it.
The card does not admit a student, place a student, set a level, or detect cheating. Filing it in the {DOCS} is inside the institution. A wording change voids the filing.

The open day, the talk with a colleague at registration, and the placement conversation are not shortened. None of them is a send outside the organisation. An offer to a hospital or a public advert would be its own gated step and is not built.
The 8 already-counted hours are the check in s4 and are not subtracted again. The 4 incremental hours are rewrites when she rejects a card.
No step infers a student's emotion. The card does not monitor staff.
unknowns: Whether the open-day calendar stores session, time and place as separate fields.
Whether a colleague other than the instructor owns the ward placement rule.
research_questions: What share of open-day cards she rejects because a session moved after she read the calendar.

already_counted.description: Checking the session, time and place against the dates and the ward rule is already in s4.

incremental.description: Rewriting a rejected open-day card herself, beyond the check already in s4.

approvals.approved_version: Open-day card she accepted in s4: session, time and place from the dates she read, plus the ward rule she read, with no named student and no admission or placement. A wording change voids it.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On an open day she rejects the card, only filing is shorter, about 3. On an open day the dates are stable, writing the card and filing it are shorter, about 8. The 4 hours of rewrites are already off the central 14.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Her week stays on the ward, the committee, the skills lab and the open day. She accepts the hours sheet, the committee brief, the supply order and the open-day card before each is filed or sent. She does not hand over patient care, the committee view, the item choice, or the placement conversation.
skills_to_grow: Check an hours sheet against the roster and reject any patient name or diagnosis.
Check a committee brief copies the decision asked and adds no vote or sanction.
Check a supply order matches the item, quantity and code she selected before it is sent.
Check an open-day card names no student and does not admit or place anyone.
role.ambitious_version: The only changes are the hours sheet, the committee brief, the supply order and the open-day card. Each is filed or sent only after she accepts that version. Patient care, the committee view, the item choice and the placement talk stay hers.
